text: The timer version label in force behind a warning or a breach reaches the ledger exactly as the case side records it, and this service neither formats nor validates it beyond the 20-character column; the placeholder of section 8 stands until the label scheme is fixed.
why: The legacy story requires the version on every timer entry, and no source names the label or its scheme, so the story writes the placeholder rather than a value.
read: RWB-E1-028 BR9, AC2, AC11, section 13; TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-005; FSD P7 A2.3
impact: Every warning and breach entry of a case; fixing the label is a data and parameter change, not a code change in this service

text: A breach entry carries its escalation role and escalation level in actions (DF-DEC-014) as escalateToRole and escalationLevel, and its decision code is the timer code the writer story fixes in LOV-DECISION.
why: TSD P7 T3.1 has no column for an escalation role or a level and LOV-DECISION has no timer value, so the two values have to ride in the JSON field until the schema and the list are extended.
read: TSD P7 T3.1 decision_log_entry; FSD P7 A2.14.3.2; RWB-E1-028 AC2
impact: The read of a breach and the auditor's reproduction of it; the store story and the writer story must carry the same shape

text: The case read of the ledger returns the deadline decisions in decided_at order and each item carries its chainSeq, so a reader sees both orders, and the chain check keeps chain_seq order.
why: This work package fixes decided_at order while FSD P3 A2.37 and legacy RWB-E2-005 fix chain_seq order, and the two differ when a record is decided before it is appended.
read: FSD P3 AC-P3-037-01 and AC-ALT-P3-037-01; legacy RWB-E2-005 steps 3 and 4; this work package
impact: SCR-38 and the deadline panel of SCR-03; no stored value changes, and the read story must declare the same order
